plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE (STAR/featureCounts, n=3)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level raw integer count matrix from STAR + featureCounts (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 6 sample columns, first column gene symbol) with a 6-row sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv) declaring one condition column: 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question is purely 'which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control', so the plan stops at the gene list plus its diagnostics — no enrichment, no deconvolution, no unasked scope.

Because the counts come from an aligner plus a counter and not from a transcript quantifier, they enter the negative-binomial model as raw integers: no tximport, no gene-length correction, no pre-scaling. Normalization stays inside the model as median-of-ratios size factors. The one thing the aligner+counter route costs is the quantifier's bias model, so T1S1 adds an explicit GC-content and gene-length bias diagnostic (log count ratio of each sample against the median sample versus GC and length); the correction tools of record (cqn, EDASeq) are not installed, so if a trend appears the step reports it as a caveat on the DE result rather than silently correcting.

T1S1 does sample-structure QC on the blind VST — PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes — which is the only chance to see a mislabelled or outlying sample before a test with three replicates per group. T1S2 runs the primary test: pre-filter at >=10 counts in >=3 samples (the smallest group size), design ~condition with the reference level set explicitly to the control level named in metadata.csv, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering left on, and the p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment is trusted. T1S3 repeats the contrast with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on TMM factors as an independent second method; at n=3 the two count models agree on most genes but not all, and the intersection is the defensible high-confidence set. T1S4 assembles the report: the intersection and the method-specific genes, the MA and dispersion diagnostics, the count-outlier NAs that DESeq2 sets at fewer than seven replicates per cell, and — stated before the gene tables — the power limit of three versus three, where the test recovers only a minority of true effects and mostly those with large fold changes, so absence from the list is not evidence of no change. Thresholds are not loosened to compensate.

Low count filter: at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples
Median-of-ratios size factors inside DESeq2, with GC/length bias diagnostic
~ condition with explicit reference level control, contrast condition treated vs control; power statement
Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness second method with TMM normalization
Report: method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, MA and dispersion plots, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, power statement, sessionInfo
